title: Cleveland 1916.1600 - 15th-century sword with wheel pommel
author: claude
summary: The baseline: wheel pommel, straight cross, leather grip, nothing else. Anything we add to a European sword should be measured against how strong this plain silhouette already is.

path: References/Museum/Cleveland 1974.58 - Hand-and-a-half sword with side ring.md
title: Cleveland 1974.58 - Hand-and-a-half sword with side ring
author: claude
summary: Long straight quillons with flared tips, a side ring guarding the hand, a faceted pear pommel, a sharkskin grip. The side ring is a functional detail that makes the hilt memorable.

path: References/Museum/Met 23352 - Sword with scabbard mounts ca. 600.md
title: Met 23352 - Sword with scabbard mounts ca. 600
author: claude
summary: A ring pommel, and a long slim scabbard articulated by metal bands and suspension mounts. The bands give the scabbard rhythm without surface decoration.

path: References/Museum/Met 24378 - Katana mounting with pampas-grass lacquer.md
title: Met 24378 - Katana mounting with pampas-grass lacquer
author: claude
summary: Restraint done right. The scabbard is plain black lacquer except for one motif: pampas grass in gold maki-e (lacquer with sprinkled gold). The pale green braided cord is the only accent color. The scabbard tip has a metal cap.

title: Met 25653 - Warring States bronze sword
author: claude
summary: The ancestor of the jian: a ridged straight blade, a solid hilt with two raised rings, a broad short guard. Green-brown patina. Every detail is structural.

path: References/Museum/Met 26069 - Shakudo collar with fish-roe ground.md
title: Met 26069 - Shakudo collar with fish-roe ground
author: claude
summary: Ornament through texture. The background is nanako: rows of tiny raised dots. Gold figures sit on top. Shakudō is a black-violet copper-gold alloy, and black with gold is a classic contrast pair.

path: References/Museum/Met 27929 - Double sword sharing one scabbard.md
title: Met 27929 - Double sword sharing one scabbard
author: claude
summary: Two flat-backed swords nest together in one scabbard and are drawn as a pair. Cloud-shaped gilt guards, wooden grips, sharkskin scabbard with gilt bands.

path: References/Museum/Met 27932 - Jian with jade hilt and green sharkskin scabbard.md
title: Met 27932 - Jian with jade hilt and green sharkskin scabbard
author: claude
summary: Three materials, each doing one job: pale jade hilt, green-dyed sharkskin scabbard, gold fittings. Luxurious without a single gem or engraving covering the surface.

title: Met 894754 - Itomaki-tachi slung sword mounting
author: claude
summary: The upper scabbard is wrapped in the same braided thread as the grip (itomaki means thread-wrapped), so the sword and scabbard read as one object by construction, not by matching paint. Gold-flecked lacquer below, openwork guard, and hanger
